exposure: Mode of birth (Caesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
cohort: The study included 379 women (291 undergoing Caesarean section and 88 vaginal delivery) from whom blood samples were collected immediately after umbilical cord clamping.
finding: No cases of clinically significant hyperfibrinolysis (LY30 > 8%) were observed immediately postpartum in women without hemorrhage.
mod_finding: LY30 values were significantly higher in vaginal deliveries compared to Caesarean sections.
